elements.label: 3D character (Oscar) at the microphone, enlarged by the snap zoom; eyes go from half-open to closed
'THE MASTER' poster on an easel, pushed partly out of frame left by the zoom

sfx_review.label: swoosh_reverse
sfx_review.note: Faint swell over the zoom that ends at about 40.0 s, just after the push-in settles; consistent with a reverse swoosh but quiet under the music.

pattern.description: A fast snap push-in (about 1.28x scale over about 4 frames) on the 3D character at the mic, cutting the poster off at the left edge, timed to the end of his name 'Oscar.' before the next line.
pattern.why_premium: A sitcom-style snap zoom does the comedic beat in about 130 ms with no new assets. The character's eyes close in the same moment, which sells the smug reaction.

build_hint.gsap: Wrap the scene in a camera container: gsap.to(camera, {scale: 1.28, x: '-2%', y: '-4%', duration: 0.13, ease: 'expo.out', transformOrigin: '60% 40%'}); swap the eye sprite or texture to closed at the same time with tl.set(eyes, {...}, '<').
build_hint.remotion: scale = interpolate(frame, [start, start + 4], [1, 1.28], {easing: Easing.out(Easing.exp), extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}) applied to an AbsoluteFill wrapper with a matching translate; a Sequence swaps the eye state on the same frame.

notes: Camera verdict push_in (scale 1.277); motion is almost all camera, not element animation. The pattern is a UI id applied to a 3D/live-style scene because it is the closest canonical one. b03-b07 are thin slivers at the right edge (curtain folds) and are not listed.
